\newcommand{\ChartFigure}[2]{%
  \begin{figure}[H]\centering
    \IfFileExists{#1}{\resizebox{\textwidth}{!}{\input{#1}}}%
      {\fbox{\parbox{0.9\textwidth}{\centering\small
        Figure \texttt{\detokenize{#1}} not generated.\\
        Run \texttt{plots/kalman\_tfg\_carma/draw\_plots.sh}.}}}
    \caption{#2}
  \end{figure}%
}

\title{TFG-CARMA3 Filter --- Wave Simulation Charts\\
\large (experimental; companion to \texttt{kalman\_tfg\_carma.pdf})}
\author{Mikhail Grushinskiy}
\date{2026}

\begin{document}
\maketitle
\input{../simulation-dataset.tex-part}

Charts for the deterministic replays of the experimental TFG-CARMA3 filter
in \texttt{src/kalman\_carma} (CARMA(4,1) on $x$, $y$ and $z$ on the
right-invariant two-frame Lie group, full reset transport) on the low, medium
and high PM--Stokes and JONSWAP records, in the figure order of the CARMA3 and
OU-III chart galleries, so the galleries compare page by page. Each record is
a twenty-minute replay of \texttt{tests/kalman\_tfg\_carma/tfg\_carma3-sim}
with the default seeds; the simulator shares CARMA3's dataset adapter, so the
two galleries differ only in the estimator. The tracking charts show the final
\SI{60}{s}; the operating-point, bias and direction charts show the whole
replay, because they are about convergence. RMS figures annotated on the
tracking charts are taken over the scored \SI{900}{s} window, so they agree
with the results table below.

The filter is a research prototype, not the shipping estimator. The CARMA
shapes are placed on the frequency $1/(2\tau_{\mathrm{applied}})$; the
harness column that OU-III uses for $r_S$ carries the vertical frequency
scale $\kappa_z$ here.
